paper_title: Fluorine Tuning of Morphology, Energy Loss, and Carrier Dynamics in Perylenediimide Polymer Solar Cells

knowledge_points.content: The fluorine-rich PBDTTF-FTTE:Ph(PDI)3 solar cells achieve a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 9.10%, with an open-circuit voltage (VOC) of 1.058 V, short-circuit current (JSC) of 15.31 mA/cm², and a fill factor (FF) of 56.18%.
knowledge_points.evidence: The champion PBDTTF-FTTE:Ph(PDI)3 blend PCE achieves 9.10% (Figure 2B)... Table 1: Voc (v) 1.058 (1.058), Jsc (mA cm-2) 14.66 (15.31), FF (%) 56.36 (56.18).

knowledge_points.content: The energy loss (Eloss) for PBDTTF-FTTE:Ph(PDI)3 devices is 0.59 eV, which is significantly lower than the 0.78 eV observed for the PBDTT-FTTE:Ph(PDI)3 analogue and ranks among the lowest reported for polymer solar cells.
knowledge_points.evidence: the energy loss (Eloss) calculated from Eg - eVoc is 0.59 eV for PBDTTF-FTTE:Ph(PDI)3, which is significantly lower than 0.78 eV for the PBDTT-FTTE:Ph(PDI)3-based devices.

knowledge_points.content: The 3D twisted perylenediimide acceptor Ph(PDI)3 was synthesized using a two-step halogen lamp photocyclization method involving iodine as a catalyst in dichloromethane and toluene.
knowledge_points.evidence: Ph(PDI)3 was synthesized by a new two-step halogen lamp photocyclization method, first illuminating compound 1 in CH2Cl2 with catalytic amount of I2 and then evaporating the CH2Cl2, redissolving in toluene, and illuminating with additional I2.

knowledge_points.content: Fluorination of the PBDTT-FTTE backbone to create PBDTTF-FTTE lowers the HOMO energy level from -5.07 eV to -5.32 eV, facilitating a higher open-circuit voltage (VOC) in bulk-heterojunction devices.
knowledge_points.evidence: estimated HOMO/LUMO levels lying at -5.07/-3.45, -5.32/-3.67... respectively (Figure 1C). The larger VOC of PBDTTF-FTTE:Ph(PDI)3 vs PBDTT-FTTE:Ph(PDI)3 is consistent with the FMO energetics.

knowledge_points.content: Optimal bulk-heterojunction (BHJ) film performance for both PBDTT-FTTE and PBDTTF-FTTE donors paired with Ph(PDI)3 is achieved using a 1:1 mass ratio in additive-free o-dichlorobenzene solvent.
knowledge_points.evidence: optimal BHJ films are achieved by blending PBDTT-FTTE or PBDTTF-FTTE with Ph(PDI)3 in a 1:1 mass ratio in additive-free o-dichlorobenzene.

knowledge_points.content: The PBDTTF-FTTE:Ph(PDI)3 blend exhibits more balanced charge transport than its fluorine-poor counterpart, with a hole-to-electron mobility ratio (μh/μe) of 1.42 compared to 14.29 for the PBDTT-FTTE blend.
knowledge_points.evidence: the hole to electron transport ratio, μh/μe, increases by 10-fold (14.29 to 1.42) in the PBDTTF-FTTE:Ph(PDI)3 blend. The enhanced μe and therefore more balanced charge transport in the PBDTTF-FTTE:Ph(PDI)3 blend are consistent with the superior FC extraction.

knowledge_points.content: TEM analysis reveals that PBDTTF-FTTE:Ph(PDI)3 blends exhibit higher-purity donor and acceptor domains and better phase separation compared to the more homogeneous/mixed morphology of the PBDTT-FTTE:Ph(PDI)3 blend.
knowledge_points.evidence: the PBDTTF-FTTE:Ph(PDI)3 blends clearly show better separated polymer/acceptor domains, while the PBDTT-FTTE:Ph(PDI)3 blend reduced contrast indicates a more homogeneous/mixed morphology. Thus, fluorine-rich PBDTTF-FTTE more effectively templates the BHJ morphology.

knowledge_points.content: Femtosecond transient absorption (fsTA) spectroscopy shows that both PBDTT-FTTE and PBDTTF-FTTE blends exhibit ultrafast electron transfer with a time constant of less than 500 fs.
knowledge_points.evidence: Ultrafast electron transfer is observed in each blend, with the fastest component having a time constant < 500 fs, far faster than previously reported (3 ps).

knowledge_points.content: Light intensity dependence measurements yield an alpha (α) value of 0.959 for PBDTTF-FTTE:Ph(PDI)3, indicating significantly reduced bimolecular recombination compared to the PBDTT-FTTE:Ph(PDI)3 blend (α = 0.862).
knowledge_points.evidence: Plots of the PBDTT-FTTE:Ph(PDI)3 and PBDTTF-FTTE:Ph(PDI)3 blends yield α values of 0.862 and 0.959, respectively... Thus, there is significantly less BR loss in the PBDTTF-FTTE:Ph(PDI)3 devices.

knowledge_points.content: DFT calculations for PBDTTF-FTTE tetramers reveal nearly antiparallel orientations (θeg ≈ 132.78°) between ground-state (pg) and excited-state (pe) dipoles, which is theorized to lower exciton binding energy and increase free charge lifetimes.
knowledge_points.evidence: PBDTTF-FTTE trimer and tetramer show antiparallel ground- and excited-state dipole orientations, ideal for exciton scission... PBDTTF-FTTE tetramer θeg (deg) 132.78.

knowledge_points.content: The cis-inward orientation of the FTTE units in the polymer backbone causes curvature that can depress hole mobility due to increased disorder, explaining the lower hole mobility in PBDTTF-FTTE compared to PBDTT-FTTE.
knowledge_points.evidence: We attribute this change in dipole orientation to the backbone curvature of the cis inward-oriented FTTE units... Pronounced curvature in polymer backbones is known to depress hole mobility due to suboptimal film morphologies and increased disorder. This may explain the modest PBDTTF-FTTE:Ph(PDI)3 μh = 13.9 x 10^-4 vs PBDTT-FTTE:Ph(PDI)3 μh = 30.9 x 10^-4.

knowledge_points.content: GIWAXS data indicates that both neat polymer films and their BHJ blends with Ph(PDI)3 are largely amorphous, with no significant correlation found between crystallographic parameters and device performance.
knowledge_points.evidence: Overall, the GIWAXS results indicate that the neat and BHJ blend films are largely amorphous, with no obvious correlation between crystallographic parameters, mobilities, and PSC performance metrics.
